title: Master Guide to Macro-Economy & Indian Economic Concepts for Banking Mains

concepts.definition: The total monetary or market value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's domestic borders in a specific time period (usually one financial year).
GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). Measures the economic output generated by permanent residents/nationals of a country anywhere in the world.

concepts.term: Net National Product (NNP) at Factor Cost
concepts.definition: Known as National Income (NI). NNP at Factor Cost = NNP at Market Price - Indirect Taxes + Subsidies.

GVA measures the contribution to an economy by an individual producer, industry, or sector. GVA at Basic Prices = GVA at Factor Cost + Production Taxes - Production Subsidies. GDP at Market Price = GVA at Basic Prices + Product Taxes - Product Subsidies.

Nominal GDP is calculated at current year market prices. Real GDP is adjusted for inflation and measured at base year prices (currently Base Year 2011-12). Real GDP = (Nominal GDP / GDP Deflator) * 100.
Comprehensive measure of price inflation across all goods and services produced in the domestic economy. GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) * 100.

inflation_metrics.published_by: National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)
inflation_metrics.basket_composition: Food and Beverages (45.86%), Pan, tobacco and intoxicants (2.38%), Clothing and footwear (6.53%), Housing (10.07% - urban only), Fuel and light (6.84%), Miscellaneous (services, healthcare, transport, education - 28.32%)
inflation_metrics.exam_significance: RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) uses CPI-Combined as the official nominal anchor for the Flexible Inflation Target (4% +/- 2%).

inflation_metrics.published_by: Office of the Economic Adviser, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
inflation_metrics.basket_composition: Manufactured Products (64.23%), Primary Articles (22.62%), Fuel & Power (13.15%)
inflation_metrics.exam_significance: Measures price changes at wholesale stage. Does NOT capture services (only physical merchandise goods).

inflation_metrics.eight_core_industries: Weight: 40.27% of IIP. 1. Petroleum Refinery Products (28.04% - highest), 2. Electricity (19.85%), 3. Steel (17.92%), 4. Coal (10.33%), 5. Crude Oil (8.98%), 6. Natural Gas (6.88%), 7. Cement (5.37%), 8. Fertilizers (2.63% - lowest).
inflation_metrics.exam_significance: Frequently asked in SBI/IBPS: Highest core sector weight (Refinery Products) and lowest (Fertilizers).

budget_deficits.significance: Total borrowing requirement of the Government from all sources (domestic markets, RBI, external). Direct gauge of macroeconomic stability.
Indicates government borrowing to finance day-to-day administrative consumption rather than capital asset creation.
Reflects the borrowing requirement needed for current fiscal policies, excluding past debt legacy interest obligations.

budget_deficits.formula: Revenue Deficit - Grants for Creation of Capital Assets
budget_deficits.significance: Adjusts for central revenue transfers to states that are used to build permanent physical infrastructure.

frbm_act.name: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003
frbm_act.key_amendments: Amended post N. K. Singh Committee Report (2017)
frbm_act.statutory_targets: Central Government Debt-to-GDP ratio of 40%, General Government (Centre + States) Debt-to-GDP of 60%, Fiscal Deficit target of 3.0% of GDP. Includes an 'Escape Clause' of up to 0.5% during national security crisis, war, or severe economic shock.

balance_of_payments.definition: A systematic record of all economic transactions conducted between residents of a country and the rest of the world during a specified period.

accounts.components: 1. Merchandise Trade (Exports - Imports of goods), 2. Invisibles (Services exports like IT/BPO, Net Transfers like worker remittances, and Net Income like dividends/interest).
accounts.cad: Current Account Deficit (CAD) occurs when imports of goods, services, and transfers exceed exports. Financed by capital account surpluses or forex reserves.

accounts.components: 1. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI - long term, managerial control >10%), 2. Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI/FII - stock market liquid shares <10%), 3. External Commercial Borrowings (ECB), 4. External Assistance (concessional bilateral/multilateral loans), 5. Banking Capital (NRI deposits like FCNR, NRE, NRO).

balance_of_payments.forex_components: Foreign Currency Assets (FCA), Gold, Special Drawing Rights (SDR), and Reserve Tranche Position (RTP) in IMF. Custodian: RBI (Section 40, RBI Act 1934).
